proposal:
# Re-rank proposal 12 (D148, loop boundary after cards 208, 209 and 219): the corrective cards go first because only they can start

- Led by: the product manager seat (fresh context, pm-rerank-12). Claude seat because the probes at 00:34 UTC show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl: codex exit 1, copilot has_quota=False remaining=-5, grok 402 Payment Required, agy individual quota reached).
- Trigger: loop boundary after the fresh-probe seat gate (208), the retro-only removal refusal (209) and the record-order fix (219) closed; their records landed in db1340b, closed in 1802d34, MOB.md regenerated in dc19ae4; the held-record blocker is resolved. The product owner's one-card waiver of the stop-the-line gate for the record-order fix (D162) ended when it closed, so the gate applies to every card again.
- Why a window and not a full Decider (D153): a loop-boundary re-rank is on the closed L1 list, it is not a one-way door (the order is re-ranked again at the next boundary) and it changes no standing rule. Note: no window counts toward the D153 experiment until the checker rule for windows is on main (that rule is the card named below); this window is recorded anyway.
- Open failures (read from .mob/audits/last.json, audit 59, 2026-10-31 01:02 UTC; the file is not committed): three open FAILs, MD-002, MD-003, MD-010. MD-002 (the staffing finding) is only partly closed: the fresh-probe seat gate (208) covers card-mode seats, but audit flag F-070 (audits 56 and 57; it had not reached this session when the note was first drafted, the facilitator found it in the ledger) shows decision seats in decider.py still have no fresh-probe check, no rotation and no recorded reason. The facilitator filed the card for decision seats starting on a fresh probe and rotating like card seats (226); it names MD-002, so the gate starts it. This corrects the first draft, which said 208 had closed MD-002. MD-003 (the record check loopholes) is fixed by the record checker hardening card; MD-010 (no independent review of 27 mob-defaults commits) is fixed by the whole-team review card. The file lists no F-008 (the loop-runner finding) among the open FAILs, and no F-063 or F-065 (the acceptance-suite flake findings); it counts 44 open FLAGs.
- Before (note 11): the record-order fix (219, now done), 210, 211, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 217, 218, 213, 212, 215, 206, 207.
- After: decision seats start on a fresh probe and rotate like card seats (226), the record checker hardening that refuses an empty task force and empty probes (210), the whole-team review of the mob-defaults rulings commits (211), the default templates carrying the pending process rulings and the feedback-loop lens (216), the loop's corrective-card gate (220), the loop running a card in the repository its Repository line names (221), the loop's retro and re-rank steps that stop on failure (222), the per-card retro from every role (223), the re-rank by the product manager and a Decider (224), card mode reading only role lines (225), the checker rule that rejects an incomplete objection window (213), the acceptance-suite thread-pool flakes (217), the mid-card retro removal that keeps the seat until the retro (218), every mob re-ranks at every loop boundary (212), every mob reviews each previous adjustment at stand-downs and retros (215), the findings file mirroring the audit register (206), the findings file history rules (207).
- Next card: decision seats start on a fresh probe and rotate like card seats (226), in mob-defaults (decider.py); it names MD-002 as its corrective action, so the corrective-card gate starts it while the FAILs are open. The record checker hardening (210) is second.
- Rationale (one line): the three cards that name an open FAIL (decision seats on a fresh probe, record checker hardening, whole-team review) go first, the decision-seat card at the head because the whole-team review and every later window run on the decision seats it fixes, since they are the only cards the corrective-card gate lets start and closing them clears the stop-the-line that holds up the templates and loop cards (D161), and the window-rule checker moves up ahead of the flake and loophole cards because every boundary without it is a window that does not count.

## Does the loop's corrective-card gate (220) go first? No, not now

Earlier notes (9 and 10) said it arguably should once number order stopped mattering. Numbers no longer force the order (out-of-order closes are accepted by the checker), so the question is now fair. The answer, on the evidence:

1. It cannot start first. The corrective-card gate starts only a card whose issue names an open FAIL. The gate card (220) names F-008, which audit 59 does not list as an open FAIL (it is carried as a FLAG). If the facilitator reads it that way, the gate refuses its start until the FAILs close. The decision-seat card (226), the record checker hardening (210) and the whole-team review (211) name MD-002, MD-003 and MD-010, which are open FAILs, so they start.
2. It would not change what runs. The loop runner today ends the loop at any blocking finding before it picks a card. The gate card lets the runner start a card that names the blocker, but the three cards that name a blocker all live in mob-defaults, and the runner cannot yet run a card in another repository (221 does that). So running 220 first leaves 226, 210 and 211 hand-run exactly as now.
3. Its value shrinks once the FAILs close. After 226, 210 and 211 close and the auditor drops MD-002, MD-003 and MD-010, no FAIL blocks and the gate card is insurance for the next FAIL, not an unblocker. It still heads the loop-runner chain (221, 222, 223, 224, 225, then 212 and 215, which depend on 222 and 224), so it stays directly behind the templates card.

Stated condition: if the next audit shows a FAIL that no queued card names, a corrective card for it goes first and this note is re-ranked.

## What changed against note 11 and why

- Added: the decision-seat card (226) at the head. Reason for head over second: the whole-team review (211) needs a Decider with a vote from every role seat, and this very window and the next ones seat decision voters through decider.py with none of the checks the card adds; fixing the seats first means 211's Decider is the first to run under them. It depends on nothing (card 208 is done) and is independent of 210, so swapping them costs nothing if the facilitator prefers 210 first.

- Removed: the record-order fix (219), done. The fresh-probe seat gate (208) and the retro-only removal refusal (209) were already out of the order, held for records; they are now closed, so nothing remains held.
- Moved: the checker rule that rejects an incomplete objection window (213) moves from behind the acceptance-suite flakes (217) and the mid-card retro removal (218) to ahead of both, after the loop-runner chain. D153 makes it the condition for windows counting toward the experiment, and the experiment's trial scope (next 5 cards) is being spent while it waits. It is in this repository, depends on nothing, and is process work (D161). It cannot start while FAILs are open (it names none), so the move only takes effect once they close.
- Unchanged: the templates card (216) stays third, carrying the two commitments adopted in note 11 (a named red template test for the feedback-loop lens; the lens joining the card recorded in git at its ready step). The findings file cards (206, 207) stay last: audit 59 reports the findings in an external ledger, and no `.mob/findings.json` exists in this repository, so whether these two cards still describe the right work is a question for the next refinement, not for this re-rank.
- Not ranked: the acceptance-suite flake card (217) keeps its place relative to the loophole card (218) because audit 59 no longer lists the flake findings as open FAILs; if the next audit does list them, the card names an open FAIL and moves to the top group.

## Reversals stated

- The templates card (216) moves behind the loop's corrective-card gate (220) if the facilitator gate refuses its start while FAILs are open; given its source line ("not a corrective card for an open finding") it will be refused until the FAILs close, so expect it to wait.
- The decision-seat card (226) swaps with the record checker hardening (210) if the facilitator finds 226 too big for D136 at ready; 210 then starts and 226 is split.
- The window-rule checker (213) moves back behind the flake card (217) if the facilitator needs the flake fix for a green CI on 213.
- If the whole-team review (211) cannot seat a reviewer who authored none of the 27 commits, it waits and the record checker hardening (210) runs alone; the next card then does not skip to the templates card, it re-ranks.

## Board and window

- Board: no held-record cards remain; the top of Ready is 226, 210, 211, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225.
- Window rule (D153, F-054): every declared role is polled, not a quorum. Same six non-proposer seats as note 11, each in its own fresh context with its own probe reference: architect, QA engineer, backend developer, delivery lead, independent reviewer (audit lens), product manager (sign-off). The proposer seat (this note) does not vote on itself. One objection with ONE fixed condition per seat; a condition is adopted as a commitment (D145) or settled in round 2. Each step its own commit: this proposal, each reply with its probe reference, the decision. D158 pre-window checklist at .mob/records/NNN/checklist-... before the window opens (seats, caps, working directory, line endings, probes at 00:34 UTC).
- Open point for the window: should the facilitator gate read F-008 (a FLAG) as an open FAIL for starting the loop-runner cards (220 to 225)? The answer decides whether those cards wait behind 210 and 211 (this note assumes they do) or can start beside them.
